title: Breaking the Discretization Barrier of Continuous Physics Simulation Learning

problems.title: The geometric error bound needs a post-correction domain
problems.source_location: Theorem 3.1, Eqs.(15)–(16), PDF p.6; Appendix F, Eqs.(24)–(27), p.24
claim: The main display uses \(K=\lfloor(t-t_0)/\Delta\rfloor\) for time \(t\), while the proof establishes a bound on error just after correction \(K\).
analysis: Write \(e_k^+\) for corrected error. The assumptions imply \[e_{k+1}^+\le\alpha e_k^++B,\quad \alpha=\kappa e^{L_F\Delta}<1,\quad B=\kappa E_{\rm ODE}+\delta_C.\] Hence \(e_K^+\le\alpha^K e_0^++B(1-\alpha^K)/(1-\alpha)\). This is the valid recurrence proved in Appendix F.

An arbitrary-time extension needs an unfinished-flow factor. For ideal trajectory \(0\), exact learned ODE \(\dot y=y\), \(\Delta=1\), initial corrected value \(1\) and correction \(y^+=e^{-2}y^-\), the assumptions hold with \(L_F=1,\kappa=e^{-2},E_{\rm ODE}=\delta_C=0\). Post-correction errors are \(e^{-k}\), but at \(t=1/2\) the error is \(e^{1/2}>1\), exceeding Eq.(16) read literally with \(K=0\).
result: The proof’s explicit post-correction interpretation resolves the principal domain issue. The same floor-indexed bound cannot be used unchanged at arbitrary times between corrections.
repair: Label the bound as applying to \(e_K^+\). If a partial-interval residual \(E_{\rm ODE}(\tau)\) is established, use \(e(t_K+\tau)\le e^{L_F\tau}e_K^++E_{\rm ODE}(\tau)\).
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is retained where stated; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
problems.impact_rationale: Minor: this is a timing-domain clarification with explicit counterevidence in the existing proof, rather than rejection of its post-correction inequality.

problems.title: A convergent upper envelope does not force error convergence
problems.source_location: Theorem 3.1 after Eq.(16), PDF p.6; final paragraph of Appendix F, p.24
claim: The paper concludes that actual corrected error converges to the nonzero floor \(C_2=B/(1-\alpha)\).
analysis: The inequality establishes only \(\limsup_K e_K^+\le C_2\). For a smooth scalar counterexample take ideal state \(0\), zero learned ODE, \(\Delta=1\), initial state \(0\), and corrected-state map \(G(y)=\cos^2(\pi y/2)\). Its additive corrector is \(G(y)-y\). Since \(|G(y)|\le1\le |y|/2+1\), assumption (b) holds with \(\kappa=1/2,\delta_C=1\); take \(E_{\rm ODE}=0\), so \(\alpha=1/2,C_2=2\). The trajectory alternates \(0,1,0,1,\ldots\), never converging, while satisfying every displayed upper bound. The assumption controls error relative to the ideal state; it does not require pairwise contraction of \(G\).
result: Bounded long-horizon error follows conditionally, but existence of an error limit or equality to the envelope floor does not.
repair: Replace the limit claim by \(\limsup_K e_K^+\le C_2\). If \(B=0\), the existing inequality does imply convergence to zero; otherwise extra dynamical assumptions are needed.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is retained where stated; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
problems.impact_rationale: Minor: the overstatement concerns the interpretation of a valid stability bound; it does not negate conditional boundedness.

problems.title: Nonzero additive correction creates a temporal jump
problems.source_location: Section 3.2, Eqs.(11)–(12) and final inference paragraph, PDF p.5
claim: The hybrid inference strategy is said to maintain continuity and smoothness although it adds a discrete correction after each ODE interval.
analysis: Equation (12) uses the previous corrected state in a lagged residual. Let the ODE be zero and initial state \(1\); choose \(\lambda=1/2\) and an admissible constant residual \(r_\psi(1)=-1/2\). The state immediately before reset is \(1\), while immediately after it is \(3/4\). The jump is \(-1/4\). In general continuity requires the added residual to vanish at the reset. The theorem explicitly permits pre/post states, so this finding does not contradict its hybrid formulation.
result: Arbitrary-time queries and piecewise smooth ODE segments remain possible; globally continuous trajectories are not guaranteed by the printed reset construction.
repair: Describe a piecewise smooth hybrid trajectory and state which side of a reset defines a query. A continuously forced replacement would be a different method requiring its own analysis.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is retained where stated; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
problems.impact_rationale: Minor: this limits an architectural regularity claim, without measuring jumps in the trained forecasts.

problems.title: A changing four-vertex neighborhood can break spatial continuity
problems.source_location: Section 3.1, Eq.(4), PDF p.4; Section 3.3, pp.5–6; Algorithm 1, p.22; Appendix C.1, p.23
claim: Relative-position message passing over the four vertices of the query’s cell is used to support spatial continuity.
analysis: Consider adjacent cells \([0,1]\times[0,1]\) and \([1,2]\times[0,1]\). Set all vertex features at \(x=0,1\) to zero and both at \(x=2\) to one; these values can sample the smooth field \(x(x-1)/2\). Choose zero query Gabor initialization, zero positional term and bias, and first message weight \(1\). As a query crosses \(x=1\), Eq.(4) sums features of four vertices: its one-sided outputs are \(0\) and \(2\). A second residual layer with zero weight/bias is the identity, and a continuous ReLU readout preserves this nonnegative jump. Within each fixed cell the map can be continuous; neighbor-set switching is the obstruction.
result: The printed decoder does not guarantee continuity across cell boundaries. Extra interpolation in an unavailable implementation could change this conclusion, and no trained spatial discontinuity is asserted.
repair: A shared-vertex bilinear interpolation construction would enforce continuity across cell boundaries, but not necessarily differentiability. This proposed decoder change has not been validated as preserving trained performance.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is retained where stated; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
problems.impact_rationale: Minor: the example refutes an automatic continuity guarantee for the specification, while leaving empirical predictive quality unresolved.
